record.paper_title: XXX Spin Chain: from Bethe Solution to Open Problems
record.original_question: Generalize domain wall boundary conditions to other exactly solvable models in such a way that the partition function of the resulting model is still given by a determinant whose dimension is proportional to the size of the system, analogously to the determinant formula for the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions.

evidence.quote: The main feature of formula (19) is the fact that the partition function of the six vertex model with DWBC is expressed as a determinant of the size of the system. The next obvious step would be the generalization of DWBC in the case of other models such that the partition function share the same feature.

Open problem: Obtain generalizations of domain wall boundary conditions for other models such that the partition function is expressed as a determinant of a dimension proportional with the size of the system.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The six-vertex model on an N×N square lattice with domain wall boundary conditions (DWBC) — namely, with the horizontal external edges on the left and right sides of the lattice all carrying one fixed spin orientation and the vertical external edges on the top and bottom sides carrying the opposite fixed spin orientation — has a partition function Z_N which, by the Izergin–Korepin formula, can be expressed as the determinant of an N×N matrix built from the Boltzmann weights of the model (so the dimension of the determinant grows linearly with the linear size of the lattice).

Problem. Find, for exactly solvable lattice models other than the six-vertex model (for example, higher-spin vertex models, the Izergin–Korepin 19-vertex model, the eight-vertex model, IRF/face models, supersymmetric or higher-rank vertex models associated with quantum groups U_q(g) beyond sl_2, or related two-dimensional statistical mechanical / integrable models), an appropriate generalization of domain wall boundary conditions such that the resulting finite-volume partition function on an L×L lattice can be written as the determinant of a matrix whose dimension is proportional to L. Equivalently: identify boundary conditions for these models for which a determinantal representation of the partition function, with determinant dimension scaling linearly with the system size, exists, and prove such a formula.
artifact.category_tag: Domain wall boundary conditions and determinant formulas
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists: determinant representations have been established for several generalizations, including the higher-spin (spin-k/2) six-vertex model with DWBC, the Izergin–Korepin 19-vertex model at roots of unity, partial DWBC for the six-vertex model, modified rational six-vertex models, and rational Richardson–Gaudin models (Cauchy permanent). However, no uniform construction is known for arbitrary exactly solvable models, so the broad problem remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: The higher spin generalization of the 6-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions and Macdonald polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Determinant expressions for partition functions of spin-k/2 vertex models on a finite square lattice with DWBC.
status_evidence.claim: DWBC determinant formulas extended to higher-spin vertex models.

status_evidence.title: Partial domain wall partition functions
status_evidence.snippet: Two determinant expressions for partial DWBC partition functions of the six-vertex model.

status_evidence.title: The domain wall partition function for the Izergin-Korepin 19-vertex model at a root of unity
status_evidence.snippet: DWBC partition function studied for the Izergin–Korepin 19-vertex model.
status_evidence.claim: Extension of DWBC to a 19-vertex model investigated.

status_evidence.title: Modified rational six vertex model on the rectangular lattice
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized DWBC where every boundary side is a mixture of up and down spins, with explicit determinant forms.
status_evidence.claim: Further generalized boundary conditions still yield determinant partition functions in the rational case.
